title: Transitioning to docs as code: a guide for technical writers on Mac
metaTitle: Transitioning to docs as code for technical writers on Mac
description: Learn how to manage your workflow migration when transitioning to docs as code on your Mac, reducing technical debt and improving document quality.
intro: Transitioning to docs as code on your Mac helps you align your documentation process with developer workflows. This shift reduces version conflicts and keeps your content in sync with the product lifecycle.
tldr: Migration is about changing your information architecture, not just your software.
Start by auditing your existing content to determine what to keep, update, or retire.
Docs as code workflows rely on Git for version control and automated testing.
Use a phased approach to migrate your team to avoid burnout and data loss.
AI tools act as a copilot for drafting and quality checks during the move.

stats.label: Weekly time spent resolving document conflicts

blocks.text: Why transitioning to docs as code is necessary

As your product scales, legacy tools like Word or basic wikis often fail. They cannot handle complex requirements like single-sourcing or versioning. When you are transitioning to docs as code, you are moving toward a system that treats documentation like software code. This means storing content in Git, using Markdown, and running tests before publishing. This shift eliminates manual formatting tasks and makes collaboration with engineers natural.

Technical writers spend significant time on administrative tasks. When tools do not integrate well, you face version chaos and constant context switching. This consumes up to 8 hours every week just on manual conflict resolution. This burden leads to burnout. It also increases the risk of errors in your documentation. Moving to an automated workflow reduces these risks and improves data accuracy.

Before you move files, audit your current content. Identify what is outdated and what must be kept. Define your information architecture first. Topic-based authoring is more effective than any specific tool. Once your structure is set, implement a three-layer architecture. This includes a Git-based version management layer, an asset organization layer, and an AI-powered automation layer.

blocks.text: Using AI as your migration copilot

AI helps during the transition by drafting content and checking for quality. It acts as a copilot while you retain control over accuracy and structure. Never rely on AI for final approval. Use it to summarize long documents or to suggest structure changes during your migration phase.

faq.question: Is docs as code right for every team?
faq.answer: It is best for teams that have developers and writers collaborating on the same product. If your team is non-technical, a simpler CMS might be better.

faq.question: How long does a migration take?
faq.answer: It depends on the size of your library and your team's familiarity with Git. Use a phased approach to avoid disrupting your release schedule.
